subject: CardioSys POC onramp: MAP, API keys, IP allowlist & peering next steps
messages:
From: Kate Lawson <kate.lawson@cardiosys.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: DevOps Team <devops@cardiosys.com>, Procurement <procurement@cardiosys.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CardioSys POC onramp: MAP, API keys, IP allowlist & peering next steps

Hi Neha,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team is excited to move to a short evaluation. We want to lock the mutual action plan this week so our infra team can provision network access and our procurement team can start paperwork. Key asks from our side: 

- Org setup & user roles (we need a sandbox org with 2 admin seats and service account)
- API keys & short-lived credentials for the POC (30-day TTL preferred)
- IP allowlist for egress to your hosted endpoints (we need the list to update firewall rules)
- VPC peering steps for private deployment testing (we plan a single peering with our staging VPC)

I've attached a sketch of our internal timeline and a short checklist — happy to share more details. Can you confirm whether Redwood can support 30-day API key TTLs for the POC and share the expected IP ranges for peering/egress?

Also looping in DevOps and Procurement for visibility.

Thanks,
Kate
Director of Platform Engineering
CardioSys

Attachments: CardioSys_MAP_initial_timeline.xlsx (see attachment)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kate Lawson <kate.lawson@cardiosys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-03T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CardioSys POC onramp: MAP, API keys, IP allowlist & peering next steps

Hi Kate — great to hear, and thanks for the clear checklist. We're aligned on the scope. Quick answers up-front: 

- Short-lived API keys: yes — we can issue POC keys valid for 30 days scoped to the sandbox org. We'll provide a rotation script and an example service account role.
- Org & roles: we can provision a sandbox org with 2 admin seats and a dedicated service account (name it svc-cardiosys-poc) — we'll confirm provisioning ETA below.
- IP allowlist: we'll supply static egress IP blocks used for the hosted runtime and a subnet recommendation for VPC peering.
- VPC peering: supported for Private customers; for the MAP POC we can stand up a peering against your staging VPC with the standard IP/CIDR constraints.

I've attached a first-pass MAP workbook (CardioSys_MAP_draft.xlsx) and a simple network diagram (redwood_poc_onramp_diagram.png). Proposed immediate milestones: 

1) Today (May 3): share MAP draft + IP/peering requirements (attached)
2) May 5: sandbox org & initial API keys issued to svc-cardiosys-poc (neha will send keys via secure channel)
3) May 7-10: DevOps will test IP allowlist & peering; Redwood support on-call for cutover
4) May 14: POC evaluation kickoff (scripts, example workloads)

Please confirm the timeline and whether Procurement needs any additional documentation for the purchase path. If that looks good, I'll ask Marissa to open the provisioning ticket and Ben to provide the IP/CIDR details.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: CardioSys_MAP_draft.xlsx, redwood_poc_onramp_diagram.png

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, Kate Lawson <kate.lawson@cardiosys.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-04T08:02:00-07:00
Subject: RE: CardioSys POC onramp: MAP, API keys, IP allowlist & peering next steps

Kate / Neha — quick technical notes on the peering/IP side from infra: 

- Egress IPs: for hosted endpoints we will provide two /28 blocks (example: 54.214.32.0/28, 18.197.64.0/28). These are the addresses your firewall should allow for API traffic.
- Peering: if you want to test VPC peering with our private runtime, we require non-overlapping CIDR and BGP routes disabled — we'll accept a /20 from your side for the peering.
- MTU: set to 1450 on your peering interface to avoid fragmentation with the accelerated network path.
- Testing: we'll run a connectivity checklist and a short stress test (200 concurrent connections) once peering is established.

I'll prepare an infra checklist and drop it into the MAP workbook. If CardioSys wants to do a faster cutover, we can schedule a joint ops call May 6 at 10am PT.

- Ben
Principal Infrastructure Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: infra_peering_checklist.md (referenced in MAP workbook)

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Kate Lawson <kate.lawson@cardiosys.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2026-05-05T09:34:00-07:00
Subject: Re: CardioSys POC onramp: MAP, API keys, IP allowlist & peering next steps

Kate — thanks for the prompt. From a timelines/close perspective (sales ops): 

- Target POC start: May 14 (as Neha suggested).
- Expected evaluation window: 2 weeks (May 14–28) with an internal check on May 21.
- Procurement: if we receive the signed order form by May 10, we can guarantee capacity allocation for the test window.

Action items for CardioSys:
1) Confirm acceptance of the MAP draft (I can update the financial cells once Procurement shares terms).
2) Procure: upload the signed order form to the HubSpot deal (link below) or send to procurement@redwoodinference.com.
3) Ops: confirm the /20 CIDR for peering and open the firewall change window for May 7.

If you want me to escalate a short credit hold or seat allocation to ensure the test runs, say the word — we can push a short reservation to Dedicated capacity for the two-week window.

Jonas Weber
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Related link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

From: Kate Lawson <kate.lawson@cardiosys.com>

Subject: Re: CardioSys POC onramp: MAP, API keys, IP allowlist & peering next steps

All — this looks good and we approve the MAP draft with two small edits (add duration of service account keys to the security notes and include our staging CIDR 10.40.0.0/16 for peering). Procurement will upload the signed order form by May 9 (attached).

Confirming the May 6 ops call at 10am PT to run through the peering checklist. Can you send the secure API keys to svc-cardiosys-poc@cardiosys.com after the call?

Thanks,
Kate
Director of Platform Engineering, CardioSys
